What if Earth's magnetic field disappeared?
Deep below us, molten iron flows in Earth's outer core, and creates a giant invisible shield.
Without it, compasses would stop pointing north. Sea turtles and some birds that use the field to find their way would get lost.
The solar wind, a stream of charged particles from the Sun, would hit our upper atmosphere directly.
Satellites would take far more radiation damage.
And over millions of years, the solar wind could strip away some of our air and water, as scientists think happened on Mars.
The good news? The field has weakened and flipped many times before, and life survived.
